children: CoreWeave Inc. (CRWV, Financials), an Nvidia-backed AI cloud infrastructure provider, has plenty of demand. The more difficult part is affording the capability to serve it.
It has started to sell $3 billion of convertible notes, with buyers having the opportunity to acquire another $500 million.

CoreWeave also launched an at-the-market program for up to 35 million shares. At Wednesday's close, that stock would be worth around $2.92 billion, but CoreWeave will determine when and if to sell dependent on market conditions.
The funding is huge consumer obligations.
CoreWeave said it had a revenue backlog of $104.2 billion in the second quarter and later disclosed more than $25 billion in new customer commitments inked early in the third quarter.
As that demand grows, so does its infrastructure footprint.
The contracted power was around 4.2 gigawatts, up from 3.7 gigawatts at the end of June. Recent short term computing contracts were in the neighborhood of $40M per megawatt on a yearly rate.
Shares of CoreWeave plummeted more than 3% on the announcement of the funding.

Next, observe how aggressively CoreWeave taps its new equity program. But there is still a lot of demand, but now investors have to balance that growth with greater debt and potential dilution for shareholders.

title: CoreWeave's $104 billion backlog comes with a costly catch
